authority.legal_name: Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) / Abu Dhabi Mobility, Department of Municipalities and Transport, Abu Dhabi
authority.geography_type: low-lying coastal capital on a cluster of islands threaded by mangrove channels and dredged lagoons
authority.home_waters_label: Abu Dhabi's island and waterfront network

mandate.summary: ITC (Abu Dhabi Mobility) plans, regulates and integrates all public transport in the emirate — bus, taxi, and the public marine network of water taxis and ferries operated with Abu Dhabi Maritime (AD Ports Group). Public water transport is a live, growing part of its mandate.
current_priorities: Grow the public marine network (water taxis + ferries) across the island capital
Integrate marine with bus/taxi and Hafilat fare media as a feeder mode
Expand terminals (Saadiyat Marina & Ferry Terminal, Rabdan Marina inaugurated) and routes
Decarbonize mobility under UAE Net Zero 2050 and Abu Dhabi Environment Vision

policy_targets.vision: UAE Net Zero 2050; Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030; Abu Dhabi Environment Vision 2030

marine_growth.passengers: >700,000 public water-taxi and ferry passengers carried since the 2021/2022 launch
marine_growth.terminals_recent: Saadiyat Marina & Ferry Terminal and Rabdan Marina inaugurated by ITC / Abu Dhabi Maritime
marine_growth.water_taxi_stations: Yas Bay, Yas Marina, Al Bandar, Al Muneera, Al Zeina, Al Qana Marina, Louvre Abu Dhabi, Marsa Mina, Rabdan Marina, Saadiyat
marine_growth.island_ferries: Saadiyat <-> Al Aliah; Dalma Island <-> Jebel Dhanna/Mugharraq (Al Dhafra); Sir Bani Yas

policy_targets.relevance: Abu Dhabi already runs a public water-taxi and ferry network across its islands and is opening new terminals. A zero-emission foiling tier is the natural fleet upgrade — faster, quieter, low-wake through the mangrove channels, and aligned to Net Zero 2050.

precedent.headline: Abu Dhabi already runs public water taxis and island ferries across the capital — and keeps opening new terminals.

existing_marine_network.operator: Integrated Transport Centre with Abu Dhabi Maritime (AD Ports Group)
existing_marine_network.modes: Public water taxi, public ferry, island ferries
existing_marine_network.scale: >700,000 passengers carried since 2021/2022; network expanded in Oct 2025 (Yas Bay station, updated schedule)
existing_marine_network.recent_terminals: Saadiyat Marina & Ferry Terminal; Rabdan Marina
existing_marine_network.note: Public marine transport is an established, growing mode here — the proposal expands and decarbonizes it, not introduces it.

uae_internal_corridor.link: Abu Dhabi <-> Dubai (and the northern emirates)
uae_internal_corridor.stat: ~140 km road corridor between the two largest emirates; no fast public water link today
uae_internal_corridor.relevance: A domestic, within-UAE marine express is national connectivity — a long-range optional extension after the island network is proven.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a marine network Abu Dhabi already operates across its islands. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent and low-wake — ideal for the shallow mangrove channels and dredged lagoons between Yas, Saadiyat, Reem, the Corniche and Al Raha — and they advance Net Zero 2050 while widening island access.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real Abu Dhabi Maritime stations/berths during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors live water-taxi/ferry stations; extensions add real water-accessible island districts.

domestic_pairs.rationale: Live water-taxi leg across the Yas Channel between Yas Bay and Al Raha; anchor proof corridor.
Corniche to the Saadiyat Cultural District (Louvre); around the headland vs a long road loop.
Mina Zayed waterfront to Saadiyat; short cross-channel hop.
Khor Al Maqta marinas (ADNEC / Grand Mosque district); displacement / no-foil through the channel.
Dense Reem Island residential to the Corniche core; relieves the Reem bridges.
Eastern Mangroves to Yas via the channel; low-wake foiling suited to the mangrove waterway.
Mirrors the live Saadiyat <-> Al Aliah island ferry.
Hudayriat leisure island to the Corniche; coastal run bypassing the Hudayriat causeway road.

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. The Abu Dhabi<->Dubai leg is DOMESTIC within the UAE. The far-west Dalma / Sir Bani Yas / Jebel Dhanna island ferries are real but Al Dhafra-regional. Cross-Gulf legs are out of the core proposal.

links.note: Within-UAE express between Abu Dhabi and Dubai waterfronts; long-range (Quanta-LR class), optional after the island network is proven.
Mirrors the existing Al Dhafra island ferries (Dalma / Sir Bani Yas via Jebel Dhanna); long-range and operationally gated.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water and dredged channels with NO land crossings. Hand-curated waypoints required wherever mangrove flats, low bridges, port TSS or shallow sabkha would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.hazard: Maqta & Mussafah channels and low bridges
hazards.detail: Khor Al Maqta and the Mussafah channel carry low road bridges (Maqta, Sheikh Zayed, Mussafah). Legs through them must be displacement / no-foil, following the dredged centreline through the bridge spans.
Eastern Mangroves, Reem and Al Raha are threaded by shallow mangrove channels; keep all geometry in charted dredged channels, never across the mangrove or sabkha flats.
Any leg toward Yas/north-east must stay well clear of the Khalifa Port traffic separation scheme and approaches.
Marsa Mina sits beside the working Mina Zayed port; route through the marked passenger channel and respect commercial traffic separation.
The Yas <-> Al Raha water is shallow and dredged; snap entries to the channel and avoid the inter-island flats.
Reclaimed leisure islands enclosed by breakwaters; snap to marked openings, not the rock.

hazards.hazard: Abu Dhabi <-> Dubai / Al Dhafra offshore (optional links only)
hazards.detail: Long links must stay in open Gulf water clear of Khalifa Port, Jebel Ali approaches, and the western offshore oilfield exclusion zones; hand-waypoint around Saadiyat, Lulu and any reclamation.
